description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, idiom 29).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/qualbare1.pl + .perl.out / .pcl.out, qualbare2.pl):
  use JSON::PP ();
  my %j = (b => JSON::PP::true);                 ref($j{b})   perl JSON::PP::Boolean   PCL "" (the STRING "JSON::PP::true")
  my @j = (JSON::PP::true, JSON::PP::false);                  perl two Boolean objects PCL two strings
  my %k = (b => JSON::PP::true, c => 1);                      perl Boolean             PCL string
RIGHT on both: `my $t = JSON::PP::true;`, `[JSON::PP::true]`, `f(JSON::PP::true)`, `(JSON::PP::true(), 1)`, and ALL THIRTEEN positions when the sub is declared in the same file (`package Foo; sub yes {...}` then `(b => Foo::yes)`).

THE EMISSION (./pl2cl < qualbare2.pl):
  my $t = JSON::PP::true;          (p-my-= $t (p-scalar-ctx (|JSON::PP|::pl-true)))
  my @j = (JSON::PP::true, 1);     (p-array-= @j (vector "JSON::PP::true" 1))          <-- the string
  my $u = [JSON::PP::true];        (... (p-array-init (p-list-ctx (|JSON::PP|::pl-true))))
  f(JSON::PP::true);               (pl-f (p-list-ctx (|JSON::PP|::pl-true)))
So the SAME token is a call on three parse paths and a string on the paren-list path: rule 11, "count the parse paths" -- one site answers the callable question differently (#266: a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE; the two negatives differ).  perl's rule: a qualified bareword is a CALL iff the sub EXISTS at compile time (the `use` loaded the module at BEGIN time); under `use strict` the other reading is a compile error, so for valid strict Perl a qualified bareword in term position that is not followed by `=>`, `->` or `::` IS a call.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): grep Pl/PExpr.pm for where a Word followed by `,`/`)` is autoquoted inside a paren list and compare with the `[...]` path, which is right; then ask what `_bareword_callable_here` / the #266 classifier answers for `JSON::PP::true` (expected: `unknown`, because the module's declared subs do not cross the `use` -- #365 made only `()`-prototyped names cross).  Two candidate fixes, pick by measurement: (a) the paren-list site routes through the same decision as the other three paths (smallest; makes the four paths agree); (b) a used module's DECLARED SUB NAMES cross the `use` (keyed by QUALIFIED name -- #421 says the bare-name table collides across packages) so the classifier answers YES.  Probe the case it would BREAK: a class name as a bare string in a list under `no strict` -- `my @isa = (Foo::Bar, Baz::Qux)`, `@ISA = (Exporter)`, `(Foo::Bar => 1)` (left of a fat comma stays a string, always), `Foo::Bar->new` in a list, `Foo::Bar::` (trailing colons = string).

BAR: emission change => corpus-diff (every differing site probed vs perl), emission-ab over lib/**/*.pm + the CPAN board modules, gen bump + the three artifacts, gate-SET scan only if a refusal stops firing, guard rows in Pl/t/bareword-call-01.t (the 13-row table above with perl's answers, plus the breaking cases).


=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED d903618b, with a review fix 4c8595b0 (see below).

THE MEASUREMENT, not the guess: the site is PExpr's binary-only-operator
branch (a Word followed by `,`), not the paren-list path the task suspected;
it fires ONLY WITHOUT `use strict` (with the pragma `$strict_call_bop` already
reads the word as a call and all thirteen probe positions are right on the
base); and the #266 classifier answers `no` for `JSON::PP::true` because NO
table here crosses a `use` -- `declared_subs` is this file's subs and the
prototype table is keyed by the BARE name (#421), carrying only what the export
scan could read plus `()`-prototypes (#365).

So NEITHER (a) nor (b) from the task: `no` on a QUALIFIED name is ignorance,
not evidence, and the answer is the one #266's own `no` verdict already gives a
bareword standing alone as a statement -- ask the IMAGE.  Both string-making
sites mark the token through ONE helper (`_mark_unplaceable_bareword`), and a
qualified `no` emits `(p-bareword-value "NAME")`: the sub if one exists there,
perl's string otherwise.

UNCHANGED and probed (17 rows, identical to perl on BOTH trees): an UNQUALIFIED
unknown stays a string (#266), `not-yet` stays a string, a word before `=>` or
`->` stays a string, `Foo::Bar::`, `No::Such::Thing`, `CORE::length`.

REVIEW FIX 4c8595b0 (found by the final gate): the runtime lookup reached the
CLASS-NAME slot of `bless`/`tie`, breaking task #142's invariant that the
bareword and quoted spellings emit the same bytes -- and putting a sub
resolution on every bless and tie call.  `_class_name_bareword` now reads the
marked Word leaf back (the same two-shapes-one-fact reading
`_read_star_slot_bareword` makes of its own slot): the POSITION is positive
knowledge, #1996's lookup is for ignorance.  perl's own answer in that slot is
the ordinary bareword rule (a declared sub IS called) -- PCL answers the string
on both trees, pre-existing, FILED as #2015.

Bars: corpus-diff vs 268d7e00 IDENTICAL over 111 files; emission-ab --shapes
122 files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF.  Guards: 6 rows in Pl/t/bareword-call-01.t
(37 -> 43) and 2 new bless shape rows in Pl/t/parser2-01.t (195 -> 197), all
inverse-verified (scratch/s492a/inverse-guards-base268.log,
scratch/s492a/inverse-s493-classslot.log).
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday): a module-QUALIFIED bareword call with no parens, followed by `,` or `)` inside a PAREN LIST, is emitted as a STRING -- `my %h = (b => JSON::PP::true)` stores "JSON::PP::true", `(JSON::PP::true, 1)` likewise; `[JSON::PP::true]`, `f(JSON::PP::true)`, `my $t = JSON::PP::true;` and a name declared in THIS file are all right
